article.title: Big Ben: The Voice of London
paragraphs: Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell inside the clock tower at the Palace of Westminster in London. Many people use the name for the whole tower, but its official name is the Elizabeth Tower.
The tower was completed in 1859. Its clock is known for being very accurate, and the bell's deep sound can be heard across central London.
After a long repair project, the tower reopened in 2022 with its clock faces painted in their original blue and gold colors.

questions.q: What is "Big Ben" originally the name of?
questions.hint: 第1段落の最初の文 “the nickname for …” に注目。
questions.explain: “Big Ben is the nickname for the great bell” とあり、もともとは大鐘の愛称です。

questions.q: What is the official name of the tower?
questions.hint: “official name” という語を探そう。
questions.explain: “its official name is the Elizabeth Tower” と書かれています。

questions.q: What happened in 2022?
questions.hint: 最後の段落の “reopened” の意味は？
questions.explain: 長い修復工事の後、2022年に再公開されました（reopened in 2022）。

summary.model: Big Ben is the great bell in the Elizabeth Tower in London. The tower was completed in 1859 and reopened in 2022 after repairs.

trips.tip: 王室の宝石（クラウン・ジュエルズ）が見られます。人気のため、時間帯の予約が必要かは公式サイトで確認しましょう。
trips.desc: 要塞・宮殿・牢獄として使われてきた、ロンドンの歴史的な城塞。

article.title: Tower of London: A Fortress with Many Stories
paragraphs: The Tower of London stands beside the River Thames in the heart of London. William the Conqueror began building it after he became king of England in 1066. Over the centuries, it has been a royal palace, a fortress, and even a prison.

Today, visitors can see the Crown Jewels there, including crowns and swords used in royal ceremonies. Guards called Yeoman Warders, often known as Beefeaters, live in the Tower and guide visitors with stories from its long history.

The Tower is also famous for its ravens. An old legend says that if the ravens ever leave, the kingdom will fall. For this reason, the birds are looked after carefully. The site became a World Heritage Site in 1988.

questions.q: Who began building the Tower of London?
questions.hint: 第1段落の2文目を読みましょう。
questions.explain: 「征服王ウィリアム（William the Conqueror）が建て始めた」と書かれています。

questions.q: What can visitors see at the Tower today?
questions.hint: 第2段落の最初の文です。
questions.explain: 現在は「王室の宝石（Crown Jewels）」が見られます。

questions.q: Why are the ravens looked after carefully?
choices: A legend says the kingdom will fall if they leave
questions.hint: 第3段落の2文目と3文目です。
questions.explain: 「カラスがいなくなると王国が滅びる」という言い伝えがあるため、大切に世話されています。

summary.model: The Tower of London is an old fortress and palace in London. Visitors can see the Crown Jewels, and a legend says the kingdom will fall if the ravens leave.

ストーンヘンジ

article.title: The Mystery of Stonehenge
paragraphs: Stonehenge is a circle of huge standing stones on Salisbury Plain in southern England. It was built in several stages, starting about 5,000 years ago.
Some of the smaller stones came from Wales, more than 200 kilometers away. Nobody knows exactly how people moved them without modern machines.
The stones line up with the sun on the longest and shortest days of the year. Because of this, many people think Stonehenge was used as a calendar or a place for ceremonies.

questions.q: When did people start building Stonehenge?
questions.hint: 第1段落の “starting about …” を読もう。
questions.explain: “starting about 5,000 years ago” とあります。

questions.q: Where did some of the smaller stones come from?
questions.hint: “came from” の後ろに地名があります。
questions.explain: 小さめの石の一部は200km以上離れたウェールズから運ばれました。

questions.q: Why do people think it was used as a calendar?
choices: The stones line up with the sun
questions.hint: “Because of this” の “this” が指す内容は？
questions.explain: 石が夏至・冬至の太陽の向きと一直線に並ぶため、暦や儀式に使われたと考えられています。

summary.model: Stonehenge is a circle of huge stones built about 5,000 years ago. The stones line up with the sun, so it may have been a calendar.

news.headline: Bike Commuting Doubles in Central London
news.script: Good evening. Cycling in central London has reached a record high. According to a new city report, the number of people riding bikes to work has doubled in the past five years. Officials say new bike lanes and lower traffic are the main reasons. Some drivers, however, complain that the roads have become too narrow. The city plans to add fifty more kilometers of bike lanes by next year.
news.summaryJa: ロンドン中心部で自転車通勤が過去5年で倍増。新しい自転車レーンと交通量の減少が主な理由。一方で道が狭くなったと不満を持つドライバーも。市は来年までにレーンを50km増やす予定。
news.summaryEn: Bike commuting in central London has doubled in five years thanks to new bike lanes and less traffic. The city will add 50 km more lanes next year.

questions.q: How much has bike commuting increased?
questions.hint: “has doubled” が聞こえたかな？
questions.explain: “has doubled in the past five years” = 過去5年で2倍になった。

questions.q: What do some drivers complain about?
questions.hint: “complain that …” の後ろを聴こう。
questions.explain: “the roads have become too narrow” と不満を述べています。

questions.q: What does the city plan to do?
choices: Add fifty more kilometers of bike lanes
questions.hint: 最後の文 “The city plans to …”
questions.explain: 来年までに自転車レーンを50km追加する計画です。

article.title: The Eiffel Tower: From "Ugly" to Icon
paragraphs: The Eiffel Tower is the most famous symbol of Paris. It was built for the World's Fair in 1889 and designed by the company of engineer Gustave Eiffel. At first, many artists criticized the iron tower and called it ugly.
Today, about seven million people visit it every year. The tower is 330 meters tall, and visitors can take elevators or climb more than 600 steps to the second floor.
At night, the tower sparkles with thousands of lights for five minutes every hour.

questions.q: Why was the Eiffel Tower built?
choices: As a home for Gustave Eiffel
To watch ships on the river
As a radio station for the army
questions.hint: 第1段落の “built for …” に注目。
questions.explain: “It was built for the World's Fair in 1889” とあります。

questions.q: How did many artists feel about the tower at first?
choices: They did not know about it
questions.hint: “At first” から始まる文を読もう。
questions.explain: 当初、多くの芸術家が “ugly（醜い）” と批判しました。

questions.q: What happens at night?
choices: The tower changes color every day
questions.hint: 最後の段落 “sparkles” の意味は？
questions.explain: 夜は毎正時に5分間、数千の電球がきらめきます。

summary.model: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair. Once criticized, it is now the symbol of Paris and about seven million people visit it every year.

trips.tip: 屋上の展望台からは、凱旋門を中心に 12 本の通りが広がる景色が見られます。階段で上るので、歩きやすい靴で行きましょう。
trips.desc: ナポレオンの勝利を記念して建てられた、パリの象徴的な門。

article.title: The Arc de Triomphe: A Monument at the Center of Paris
paragraphs: The Arc de Triomphe stands at the top of the Champs-Élysées in Paris. Napoleon ordered it to be built in 1806 to honor the soldiers of the French army. It was finished in 1836, many years after his order.

The arch is about fifty meters tall, and twelve avenues meet around it in the shape of a star. From the top, visitors can enjoy a wide view of the city. Many people say it is one of the best places to see Paris.

Under the arch lies the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier from the First World War. A flame is lit there every evening to remember the soldiers who gave their lives. Parades and national ceremonies are often held around the monument.

questions.q: Why did Napoleon order the arch to be built?
choices: To honor the soldiers of the French army
questions.hint: 第1段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 「フランス軍の兵士たちをたたえるため」に建てるよう命じました。

questions.q: How many avenues meet around the arch?
questions.hint: 第2段落に数字が出てきます。
questions.explain: 「12 本の大通り（twelve avenues）」が星の形に集まっています。

questions.q: What happens at the tomb every evening?
questions.hint: 第3段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 亡くなった兵士たちを思い出すために、毎晩「炎（flame）」がともされます。

summary.model: Napoleon ordered the Arc de Triomphe in 1806. Twelve avenues meet around it, and a flame is lit every evening at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

trips.name: 凱旋門

trips.city: ヴェルサイユ（パリ近郊）

trips.desc: ルイ 14 世が築いた、豪華な鏡の間で知られる宮殿。

article.title: The Palace of Versailles: A Symbol of Royal Power
paragraphs: The Palace of Versailles lies about twenty kilometers southwest of Paris. It began as a small hunting lodge of Louis XIII, but his son, Louis XIV, enlarged it dramatically. In 1682, he moved the royal court there, and the palace became the center of French politics for over a century.

The most famous room is the Hall of Mirrors, a long gallery lined with hundreds of mirrors and tall windows that face the gardens. In the evening, candlelight made the room shine. In 1919, the treaty that ended the First World War was signed in this very hall.

Outside, the vast gardens were designed by André Le Nôtre, who arranged fountains, flower beds, and long paths in perfect symmetry. The palace and its gardens were added to the World Heritage list in 1979, and they attract millions of visitors every year.

questions.q: What was the Palace of Versailles at first?
questions.hint: 第1段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: もともとはルイ 13 世の小さな狩猟用の館（hunting lodge）でした。

questions.q: What is the Hall of Mirrors known for?
choices: A long gallery with many mirrors and windows
questions.hint: 第2段落の最初の文を読みましょう。
questions.explain: 多くの鏡と大きな窓が並ぶ、長い回廊です。

questions.q: Who designed the gardens?
questions.hint: 第3段落の最初の文です。
questions.explain: 庭園を設計したのは、アンドレ・ル・ノートルです。

summary.model: Louis XIV turned a hunting lodge into the grand Palace of Versailles. It is famous for the Hall of Mirrors and its large gardens, and it is a World Heritage site.

news.headline: French Bakeries Struggle with Rising Butter Prices
news.script: French bakeries are facing a difficult year. The price of butter has risen by almost thirty percent, and many bakers say they cannot keep their croissants cheap. A baker in Lyon told reporters that she now pays twice as much as two years ago. Some shops have started making smaller croissants, while others have raised prices. Customers say they will still buy them, but less often.
news.summaryJa: フランスのパン屋がバター価格の高騰（約30％上昇）に苦しんでいる。リヨンのパン職人は2年前の2倍を払っていると話す。クロワッサンを小さくする店や値上げする店も。客は買う頻度を減らすと話している。
news.summaryEn: Butter prices in France have risen by almost 30 percent. Some bakeries are making smaller croissants or raising prices, and customers will buy them less often.

questions.q: How much has the price of butter risen?
questions.hint: “thirty” と “thirteen” の聞き分けに注意。
questions.explain: “risen by almost thirty percent” = 約30％上昇。

questions.q: Where is the baker who talked to reporters?
questions.hint: “A baker in …” の地名を聴こう。
questions.explain: “A baker in Lyon told reporters …” とあります。

questions.q: What have some shops started doing?
questions.hint: “Some shops have started …”
questions.explain: 一部の店はクロワッサンを小さくし始めました。

news.headline: Toronto Adds New Bike Lanes Along the Lake
news.script: Good evening. Toronto is building new bike lanes along the edge of Lake Ontario. The city says the lanes will connect the waterfront with the downtown area. Work starts next month and should finish before winter. Many residents welcome the plan, but some shop owners worry about fewer parking spaces. The city promises to listen to their concerns.

news.summaryEn: Toronto is building new bike lanes along the lake. Work starts next month. Some shop owners worry about parking.

questions.q: Where are the new bike lanes being built?

questions.q: When should the work finish?
questions.hint: work starts next month のあとの文です。
questions.explain: 「冬になる前（before winter）に終わる予定」と言っています。

questions.q: What do some shop owners worry about?
questions.hint: worry about を探しましょう。
questions.explain: 一部の店主は「駐車スペースが減ること（fewer parking spaces）」を心配しています。

article.title: Niagara Falls: Where Water Meets Thunder
paragraphs: Niagara Falls is on the border between Canada and the United States. It is made up of three waterfalls. The biggest one is called Horseshoe Falls, because it has the shape of a horse's shoe. It is about fifty meters tall.

Millions of people visit the falls every year. Many of them take a boat tour called the Maid of the Mist. The boat goes very close to the falls, and the visitors wear raincoats because of the spray. The sound of the water is as loud as thunder.
The falls are also useful. Their strong water flow is used to make electricity for homes and factories. At night, colorful lights shine on the water, and the falls look different from the daytime.

questions.q: Where is Niagara Falls?
choices: Between Canada and the United States
questions.hint: 第1段落の最初の文です。
questions.explain: ナイアガラの滝は、カナダとアメリカの国境にあります。

questions.q: Why do visitors wear raincoats on the boat tour?
choices: Because of the spray from the falls
Because it is a rule of the city
Because the boat has no roof
questions.hint: 第2段落の3文目です。
questions.explain: 船が滝に近づくので、水しぶき（spray）でぬれるからです。

questions.q: What is the water power of the falls used for?
questions.hint: 第3段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 強い水の流れは、電気（electricity）を作るために使われています。

summary.model: Niagara Falls is made up of three waterfalls on the border of Canada and the United States. Visitors take boat tours, and the water is used to make electricity.

trips.name: ナイアガラの滝

trips.tip: 展望台の床の一部がガラスになっていて、真下が見えます。天気のよい日は、遠くのナイアガラ方面まで見えることがあります。
trips.desc: トロントの空にそびえる、高さ約 553 メートルの塔。

article.title: The CN Tower: Toronto's Tall Landmark
paragraphs: The CN Tower is a very tall tower in Toronto, Canada. It was completed in 1976 and is about 553 meters high. For many years, it was the tallest free-standing structure in the world.

The tower was built to send television and radio signals across the city. Today, it is also a popular place for tourists. A fast elevator takes visitors to the observation deck in less than a minute. There is even a glass floor, and people can look straight down at the city below.

Brave visitors can try the EdgeWalk, a walk around the outside of the tower, high above the ground. Others enjoy dinner at the revolving restaurant, which slowly turns and gives a full view of Toronto and Lake Ontario.

questions.q: When was the CN Tower completed?
questions.hint: 第1段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 塔は 1976 年に完成しました。

questions.q: What was the tower first built for?
choices: To send television and radio signals
To protect the city from floods
questions.hint: 第2段落の最初の文です。
questions.explain: テレビやラジオの電波を、街じゅうに送るために建てられました。

questions.q: What can visitors do at the top of the tower?
questions.hint: 第3段落の最初の文です。
questions.explain: 勇気のある人は、塔の外側を歩く EdgeWalk に挑戦できます。

summary.model: The CN Tower in Toronto was completed in 1976 and is about 553 meters high. Visitors can stand on a glass floor or try the EdgeWalk.

article.title: Banff National Park: A Jewel of the Canadian Rockies
paragraphs: Banff National Park is in the Rocky Mountains of Alberta, Canada. It was created in 1885 and is the oldest national park in the country. The park is known for its tall snowy mountains, thick forests, and clear blue-green lakes.

Lake Louise and Moraine Lake are two of its most famous lakes. Their color comes from tiny pieces of rock, called rock flour, which are carried into the water by glaciers. When the sunlight hits the water, the lakes shine in a beautiful turquoise.

Visitors enjoy hiking, skiing, and relaxing in hot springs. Wild animals such as elk and bears live in the park, so visitors must keep a safe distance from them. The area is part of a World Heritage Site called the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks.

questions.q: Where is Banff National Park?
choices: In the Rocky Mountains of Alberta
On the coast of Nova Scotia
questions.hint: 第1段落の最初の文です。
questions.explain: アルバータ州のロッキー山脈にあります。

questions.q: Why do the lakes look turquoise?
choices: Because of paint from the mountains
Because of tiny pieces of rock carried by glaciers
questions.hint: 第2段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 氷河が運んでくる、細かな岩の粉（rock flour）が水に混ざっているためです。

questions.q: What must visitors do when they see wild animals?
questions.hint: 第3段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 野生動物とは安全な距離（safe distance）を保つ必要があります。

summary.model: Banff National Park, created in 1885, lies in the Canadian Rockies. Its turquoise lakes get their color from rock flour carried by glaciers, and it is a World Heritage site.

article.title: Sails on the Harbour
paragraphs: The Sydney Opera House is one of the most famous buildings of the 20th century. Its roof looks like white sails on Sydney Harbour.
The Danish architect Jørn Utzon won an international design competition in 1957. However, construction was difficult and expensive, and it took until 1973 to finish.
Today, the building hosts more than 1,500 performances a year, from opera and ballet to rock concerts. In 2007, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: What does the roof look like?
questions.hint: “looks like …” は「〜のように見える」。
questions.explain: 屋根は港に浮かぶ白い帆のように見えます。

questions.q: Where was the architect from?
questions.hint: “Danish” はどこの国の形容詞？
questions.explain: “Danish” = デンマークの。建築家ウッツォンはデンマーク出身です。

questions.q: When did it become a World Heritage Site?
questions.hint: 最後の文の年号。
questions.explain: 2007年にユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。

summary.model: The Sydney Opera House has a roof like white sails. It was finished in 1973, hosts many performances, and is a World Heritage Site.

trips.desc: 宇宙からも見える世界最大のサンゴ礁。

article.title: The Great Barrier Reef in Danger
paragraphs: The Great Barrier Reef, off the coast of Queensland, is the largest coral reef system in the world. It is so big that it can be seen from space.
The reef is home to thousands of kinds of fish, as well as turtles, dolphins, and sharks. Coral is actually made of tiny living animals.
However, the reef is in danger. When the ocean becomes too warm, coral turns white and can die. This is called coral bleaching. Scientists and tourists are working together to protect it.

questions.q: What is special about the size of the reef?
choices: It can be seen from space
questions.hint: “so big that …” は「とても大きいので…」。
questions.explain: 宇宙からも見えるほど大きいサンゴ礁です。

questions.q: What is coral made of?
questions.hint: “actually made of …”
questions.explain: サンゴは実は小さな生き物（動物）でできています。

questions.q: What causes coral bleaching?
choices: Ocean water that is too warm
questions.hint: “When the ocean becomes …”
questions.explain: 海水温が高くなりすぎるとサンゴが白くなる（白化）。

summary.model: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef. Warm oceans cause coral bleaching, so people are working to protect it.

trips.city: ノーザンテリトリー（オーストラリア中央部）
trips.tip: 日の出と日没のころ、岩の色が赤く変わって見えます。現地では、先住民アナング族の文化を尊重するルールを守りましょう。
trips.desc: オーストラリア大陸の中央にそびえる、巨大な一枚岩。

article.title: Uluru: The Red Heart of Australia
paragraphs: Uluru is a huge sandstone rock in the middle of Australia. It rises about 348 meters above the flat desert, and its base is more than nine kilometers around. Many visitors travel a long way to see it with their own eyes.

The rock is sacred to the Anangu, the traditional owners of the land. For them, Uluru is not just a rock. It is connected to old stories and laws that have been passed down for thousands of years. Since 2019, climbing the rock has been banned out of respect for their culture.

Uluru is famous for changing color during the day. At sunrise and sunset, it glows deep red and orange. Visitors often gather at special viewing areas to watch this beautiful change. The area is protected as a national park and a World Heritage Site.

questions.hint: 第3段落の2文目です。
questions.explain: 日の出と日没のころに、深い赤やオレンジ色に輝きます。

summary.model: Uluru is a huge sandstone rock in central Australia. It is sacred to the Anangu, climbing it has been banned since 2019, and it glows red at sunrise and sunset.

news.headline: Young Coral Recovering Faster Than Expected
news.script: Scientists in Queensland have shared some good news about the Great Barrier Reef. In several areas, young coral is growing faster than expected after last year's bleaching. Researchers say cooler water this season helped the coral recover. However, they warn that the reef is still at risk, and that reducing greenhouse gases is the only long-term solution.
news.summaryJa: グレート・バリア・リーフで、昨年の白化の後、若いサンゴが予想以上の速さで成長している。今季の海水温が低かったことが回復を助けた。ただし研究者は、サンゴ礁は依然危機にあり、温室効果ガスの削減が唯一の長期的解決策だと警告している。
news.summaryEn: Young coral on the Great Barrier Reef is recovering faster than expected thanks to cooler water, but scientists say cutting greenhouse gases is still necessary.
